app.name: Name of the native app under its home-screen icon (iOS CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName, Android app label). The name of the trainer app, Fivvi Pro, the same in both languages.
app.title: Browser tab title (HTML <title>) of web pages that don't set their own, and the name of the client app under its home-screen icon (iOS CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName, Android app label). The product name, Fivvi, the same in both languages.
appLink.back: Accessibility label of the back button on the opened-link screen of the client app: returns to the tabs.
appLink.openInBrowser: Button on appLink.soon, in the client app: opens the same link in the phone's browser.
appLink.soon: Client app (Fivvi): the screen a join link (/j/...) or an invitation link (/i/...) opens until the join and invitation screens exist (F029, F032). Says the app will open the link itself soon.
classLevel.accessibleName: Accessible name (screen reader) and tooltip of the three-bar level icon after a class name in a list (F067): {level} is the level word of classLevel.allLevels … classLevel.advanced in the viewer's language, e.g. 'Niveau: Gevorderd'. Never shown for Geen or Alle niveaus in a list.
classLevel.advanced: Level of a class (F067): the highest of the four; three bars filled. Shown with the icon on a page about one class and as the option in the Niveau field.
classLevel.allLevels: Level of a class (F067): the class suits everyone. Option in the Niveau field and the word on a page about one class; a list shows no icon for it.
classLevel.beginner: Level of a class (F067): the lowest of the four; one bar filled. The same word in both languages.
classLevel.field: Label of the Niveau field on the class form, Nieuwe groepsles and Les wijzigen (F067): one of the five words of classLevel.*.
classLevel.intermediate: Level of a class (F067): the middle level; two bars filled. Dutch: Gemiddeld.
classLevel.none: The starting value of the Niveau field (F067): the class has no level. Dutch: Geen. A page about one class shows nothing for it, and no empty line remains.
classes.app.cancelBody: CO-03 in the apps (the native confirmation of Les annuleren): says how many booked clients get the cancellation email (EM-05). The message for the participants is written on the web only. {participants} is a count of at least 1; the case of no participants uses classes.cancel.countNone.
classes.app.cancelOffline: CO-03 in the apps: shown on the class date page while the phone is offline, where Les annuleren is disabled; nothing is queued.
classes.app.shareLink: TD-03 in the apps (F037): the button below the participants and the first item of the Owner's ⋯ menu. Gets or makes the link of this class date in the visitor's language and puts it on the clipboard.
classes.app.shareLinkCopied: TD-03 in the apps (F037): shown after Boekingslink delen has put the date's short link on the clipboard.
classes.app.shareLinkOffline: TD-03 in the apps (F037): shown on the class date page while the phone is offline, where Boekingslink delen is disabled; nothing is queued.
classes.date.changedField.level: One word in the line 'Aangepast t.o.v. de reeks: {fields}' on a class date (CO-01): the level of this date was changed on its own (F067). Lowercase; Dutch: niveau.
classes.date.typeAndLevel: The eyebrow of the class-on-a-date screen (TD-03, F067): the kind of session and the level word, e.g. 'Groepsles · Gevorderd'. {type} is the session type, {level} one of classLevel.allLevels … classLevel.advanced. Not used for Geen: the eyebrow is then the type alone.
clientNav.book: Second tab of the client app: where a client books a class. A verb in the tab bar (GLOSSARY: Book / Boeken).
clientNav.home: First tab of the client app. The same word in both languages (GLOSSARY: Home).
clientNav.label: Accessibility label of the client app's tab bar (TalkBack).
clientNav.profile: Third tab of the client app: the client's name, email address, language and sign-out.
clients.addDialog.close: Accessibility label of the close button (x) of the new-client form in the apps.
clients.newClient: Primary action of the native clients list (New client): opens the full-screen form that adds a client. Shown only to people who may manage clients.
clients.offline: Banner above the cached clients list in the apps while there is no connection. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '08:42', formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
clients.profile.back: Accessibility label of the back button of the client profile in the apps.
clients.profile.edit: Button on the client profile that opens the edit form for the overview (name, email address, language for emails).
clients.profile.editTitle: Title of the form that edits a client in the apps.
clients.profile.save: Button that saves the edited client.
clients.profile.saved: Brief confirmation (snackbar) after the edited client was saved.
clients.profile.upcomingWhen: One row of the client's upcoming sessions on the client profile: {date} is a short date such as "do 24 sep", {time} a 24-hour time.
clients.title: Title of the clients list (TM-02, TW-01) and the label of the way in to it.
common.cancel: Button that leaves a form or dialog without saving, e.g. the native full-screen dialog that changes the person's name.
common.loading: Accessibility label of the progress indicator while a screen loads (read by VoiceOver and TalkBack).
common.loadingSlow: Line under a loading placeholder that is still waiting after 10 seconds.
common.offline: Banner at the top of the client app while the phone has no connection. Not tied to one list, so it has no time (clients.offline names the time of a cached list).
common.retry: Button under an error message that tries the failed action again.
email.cancellation.intro: First sentence of the class variant of EM-05, the client's notice that a class date is cancelled (spec F026). {class} is the class name in the reader's language, {date} the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'dinsdag 20 oktober 2026', {time} the start time, e.g. '18:00'. The booking is cancelled with the date.
email.cancellation.messageFrom: Line above the message the Owner typed for the participants of a cancelled class date (class variant of EM-05). {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym). The message follows in a quoted block, as typed, and is never translated.
email.cancellation.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject of the class variant of EM-05. {class} is the class name, {date} the weekday and date without year, {time} the start time.
email.cancellation.subject: Subject of the class variant of EM-05, the client's notice that a class date is cancelled (spec F026). {class} is the class name in the reader's language, {date} the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 20 oktober'.
email.cancellation.where: Line of the class variant of EM-05 with the place. {location} is the name of the location, followed by its address when it has one.
email.emailChangeCode.ignore: Last line, for someone who did not ask for it (a mistyped address, or somebody else's): the email changes nothing by itself.
email.emailChangeCode.intro: Line above the 6-digit code, which is shown on its own line below it. The person asked to change the email address of their Fivvi account to this address.
email.emailChangeCode.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {code} is the 6-digit code.
email.emailChangeCode.subject: Subject of EM-34, the email with the code that confirms a new email address (F005, spec #610). Sent to the NEW address only.
email.emailChangeCode.validity: {minutes} is how many minutes the code works, e.g. 15. The second sentence says the new address is the one they sign in with from then on.
email.emailChangeTaken.ignore: Last line: nothing to do, the email can be ignored.
email.emailChangeTaken.intro: First line: someone asked for a code to use this address for another account; because the address already belongs to an account, no code was sent. Does not say who asked.
email.emailChangeTaken.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject.
email.emailChangeTaken.subject: Subject of EM-36, the notice that goes to an email address that already has a Fivvi account when someone asked for a code to change the address of ANOTHER account to it (F005, spec #610). It replaces the code and reveals nothing to the person asking.
email.emailChangeTaken.unchanged: Reassurance: the account of the recipient was not changed and nothing was merged.
email.emailChanged.fine: Second line, for the person who made the change themselves.
email.emailChanged.intro: First line: the address of the account was just changed; the person no longer signs in with this (the old) address but with the new one. The new address is not named.
email.emailChanged.notYou: Last line, for someone who did not make the change: contact us through the Help and contact page of fivvi.app (the page is called Help en contact in Dutch). No link and no button, so nothing in the email can undo the change.
email.emailChanged.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject.
email.emailChanged.subject: Subject of EM-35, the notice that goes to the OLD email address after the address of a Fivvi account was changed (F005, spec #610). It has no link.
email.frame.button: Label of the one primary button of a client or team email; it opens the client web (fivvi.app).
email.frame.clientReason: Footer line of every client email (the client frame, F049): why the person got it. {workspace} is the workspace's name as the owner typed it; do not change it.
email.frame.questions: Footer line under the reason in client and team emails. {workspace} is the workspace's name: the person asks the gym, not Fivvi.
email.frame.sentWith: Small last line at the bottom of client and team emails.
email.frame.teamReason: Footer line of every email to a trainer or owner (the team frame, F049): why the person got it. {workspace} is the workspace's name as the owner typed it.
email.hello.greeting: {firstName} is the recipient's first name. When unknown, use email.hello.greetingWithoutName.
email.hello.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject.
email.hello.sentAt: {date} is a weekday and date with year, e.g. 'dinsdag 29 september 2026'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
email.hello.subject: Subject of the test email that checks email delivery (E006). Only sent by the team, never to clients.
email.layout.footer: Last line of every email, below the content.
email.privateSession.intro: First sentence of EM-11. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym) where the session is planned.
email.privateSession.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {date} is the weekday and date without year, {time} the start time.
email.privateSession.subject: Subject of EM-11, the email that confirms a new private session to the client. {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september', {time} the start time, e.g. '09:00'. 'Afspraak' is used in this subject only; everywhere else the product says 'privésessie'.
email.privateSession.trainer: Line of EM-11 and EM-04 with the person who teaches. {Word} is the workspace's word for them with a capital start (F068), e.g. Instructeur / Instructor; {trainer} is the person's name and stays a name. Left out when the trainer has no name.
email.privateSession.when: Line of EM-11 with the time of the session. {date} is the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september 2026'; {start} and {end} are the start and end time, e.g. '09:00' and '10:00'.
email.privateSession.where: Line of EM-11 with the place. {location} is the name of the location, followed by its address when it has one.
email.privateSessionCancelled.intro: First sentence of the private-session variant of EM-05. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym) where the session was planned.
email.privateSessionCancelled.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject of the private-session variant of EM-05. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym).
email.privateSessionCancelled.subject: Subject of the private-session variant of EM-05, the client's notice that their private session is cancelled (spec F026). {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september', {time} the start time, e.g. '09:00'. Says 'sessie', like EM-04; 'afspraak' is used in the subject of EM-11 only.
email.privateSessionCancelled.when: Line of the private-session variant of EM-05 with the time the session had. {date} is the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september 2026'; {start} and {end} are the start and end time, e.g. '09:00' and '10:00'.
email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime: A weekday, date and time inside the subject and the preview of EM-04. {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september'; {time} the start time, e.g. '09:00'.
email.privateSessionMoved.intro: First sentence of EM-04. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym) where the session is planned.
email.privateSessionMoved.now: Line of EM-04 with the new time. {date} is the weekday and date with year; {start} and {end} are the start and end time.
email.privateSessionMoved.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject of EM-04. {newDate} is the new day and time, built with email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime.
email.privateSessionMoved.previously: Line of EM-04 with the time before the move. {date} is the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september 2026'; {start} and {end} are the start and end time.
email.privateSessionMoved.subject: Subject of EM-04, the email that tells the client a private session moved. {newDate} is the new day and time, built with email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime, e.g. 'vrijdag 25 september om 10:00'. Only the new date: with both the subject passed 78 characters (F049). Says 'sessie' here, as the spec words it; the UI says 'privésessie'.
email.signIn.ignore: Last line of the sign-in email, for someone who did not ask for it.
email.signIn.intro: Line above the 6-digit sign-in code, which is shown on its own line below it.
email.signIn.linkButton: Label of the button that opens the sign-in link (the confirmation page).
email.signIn.linkIntro: Line above the sign-in link. The link opens a confirmation page; nothing is signed in until the person presses its button.
email.signIn.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {code} is the 6-digit sign-in code.
email.signIn.subject: Subject of EM-08, the sign-in email. Contains the code and a sign-in link (inloglink).
email.signIn.validity: {minutes} is how many minutes the code and the sign-in link work, e.g. 15.
email.trainerChange.classDatesPreview: Preview text of EM-13 when several dates of a class change trainer. {class} is the class name, {date} the first date without year, {word} the workspace's word for the role (F068).
email.trainerChange.classDatesSubject: Subject of EM-13, the client's notice of a new trainer, when SEVERAL dates of a class are affected (Deze en alle volgende lessen): one email lists them all. {class} is the class name in the reader's language, {date} the first affected date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 13 oktober'.
email.trainerChange.classIntro: First sentence of EM-13 for a class. {word} is the workspace's word for the role (F068), {class} the class name and {workspace} the name of the workspace (the gym).
email.trainerChange.classPreview: Preview text of EM-13 when one date of a class changes trainer. {class} is the class name, {date} the date without year, {word} the workspace's word for the role (F068).
email.trainerChange.classSubject: Subject of EM-13, the client's notice of a new trainer, when ONE date of a class is affected. {class} is the class name in the reader's language, {date} the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 13 oktober'. {word} is the workspace's word for the role (F068), e.g. trainer.
email.trainerChange.dateElsewhere: One line of the date list of EM-13 for a date that is held somewhere other than the usual place: the same as email.trainerChange.dateLine plus {location}, the place's name and address.
email.trainerChange.dateLine: One line of the date list of EM-13 when several dates changed. {date} is the weekday and date with year; {start} and {end} are the start and end time, e.g. '18:00' and '19:00'.
email.trainerChange.datesIntro: Line above the list of dates in EM-13, when more than one date of a class changed trainer.
email.trainerChange.nothingElse: Last line of EM-13: the booking, the time and the place are as they were.
email.trainerChange.privateIntro: First sentence of EM-13 for a private session. {word} is the workspace's word for the role (F068), {workspace} the name of the workspace (the gym).
email.trainerChange.privatePreview: Preview text of EM-13 for a private session. {date} is the weekday and date without year, {word} the workspace's word for the role (F068).
email.trainerChange.privateSubject: Subject of EM-13, the client's notice that the trainer of their private session changed (owner decision, 4 November 2026). {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september'. {word} is the workspace's word for the role (F068), e.g. trainer.
email.trainerChange.trainerNow: Line of EM-13 that names the new trainer. {trainer} is the person's name and stays a name. Left out when the trainer has no name.
email.trainerChange.when: Line of EM-13 with the time of the session or class date. {date} is the weekday and date with year; {start} and {end} are the start and end time.
email.trainerChange.where: Line of EM-13 with the place. {location} is the name of the location, followed by its address when it has one.
email.trainerInvitation.button: Label of the button that opens the invitation page, where the person accepts or declines.
email.trainerInvitation.ignore: Last line of EM-09: the person can ignore the email when it is unexpected.
email.trainerInvitation.intro: The one sentence of EM-09. {inviter} is the name of the Owner who invites, {workspace} the name of the workspace; the person is invited to join its team to teach there. {aWord} is the workspace's word for the people who teach with its article, lowercase (F068): 'een instructeur' / 'an instructor' (English chooses a or an).
email.trainerInvitation.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {workspace} is the name of the workspace. {aWord} is the workspace's word for the people who teach with its article, lowercase (F068): 'een instructeur' / 'an instructor' (English chooses a or an).
email.trainerInvitation.subject: Subject of EM-09, the email that invites a trainer to a workspace. {inviter} is the name of the Owner who invites, {workspace} the name of the workspace.
email.trainerInvitation.validity: {date} is the last day the invitation works, a weekday and date with year, e.g. 'vrijdag 13 november 2026', in the workspace's time zone.
hello.greeting: Greeting above the home screen. {name} is the user's first name.
hello.nextSession: {date} is a weekday and date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 22 september'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
hello.sessionsToday: Number of sessions the trainer has today, 1 or more. For 0, use hello.noSessionsToday.
home.openWeb: Button under home.setUpOnWeb in the native apps; opens Fivvi on the web (the first-run screen) in the phone's browser.
home.setUpOnWeb: Native home when the account has no workspace but may set one up. Creating a workspace happens on the web only; this line tells the person to do that. Above home.openWeb.
home.signedInAs: Native apps only: line on the signed-in home placeholder that says which account is signed in. {email} is the account's email address, shown in full to its owner.
home.tab: Label of the tab that holds the workspace home (Klanten, Profiel and the account) in Fivvi Pro.
myCalendar.app.clockBack: Note on Agenda (iOS and Android) for the day the clocks go back (autumn). {day} is the short date, e.g. 'zo 25 okt'.
myCalendar.app.clockForward: Note on Agenda (iOS and Android) for the day the clocks go forward (spring). {day} is the short date, e.g. 'zo 29 mrt'.
myCalendar.app.dots: Spoken name of the dots under a day of the week strip or the month grid: how many sessions the day has (cancelled ones not counted).
myCalendar.app.failed: Banner on Agenda when the sessions of the shown week or month could not be read.
myCalendar.app.nextMonth: Accessibility label of the arrow to the next month on the month grid.
myCalendar.app.nextWeek: Accessibility label of the arrow to the next week on the week strip.
myCalendar.app.now: Accessible name of the now-line on the timeline of Agenda's Day view; {time} is the time now, e.g. '08:35'.
myCalendar.app.previousMonth: Accessibility label of the arrow to the previous month on the month grid.
myCalendar.app.previousWeek: Accessibility label of the arrow to the previous week on the week strip.
myCalendar.app.tab: Label of the second tab of Fivvi Pro: the trainer's calendar across workspaces.
myCalendar.app.todayHeading: Heading of today in the week list of Agenda, {date} is the long date.
myCalendar.app.viewMonth: Segment of the control Dag | Week | Maand on Agenda.
myCalendar.app.weekLine: Line under the week strip: the ISO week number and the range, e.g. 'Week 43 · 19 okt – 25 okt 2026'. {range} is built from myCalendar.range.
myCalendar.block: The first line of a calendar block and the start of its spoken name: the session type in words, a dot, then the client or class name, e.g. 'Privé · Anna' or 'Groep · Kracht'. The type always comes first (colour is never the only signal).
myCalendar.blockBooked: Places taken and capacity of a group class on its block, e.g. '3/8'.
myCalendar.clockBack: Tooltip and screen-reader note on the day header of the day the clocks go back (autumn).
myCalendar.clockForward: Tooltip and screen-reader note on the day header of the day the clocks go forward (spring).
myCalendar.optionGroup: Checkbox in the Type filter: show group classes.
myCalendar.optionPrivate: Checkbox in the Type filter: show private sessions.
myCalendar.range: A range of dates, such as '21 sep – 27 sep 2026' (day and short month, the end with the year). {start} and {end} are formatted in code.
myCalendar.showCancelled: Checkbox in the Type filter: show cancelled sessions (on by default).
myCalendar.timeRange: Start and end of a session as 24-hour times without spaces, '09:00–10:00'.
myDay.app.freeGapLength: Length of the free gap in hours, {hours} is a number such as 1,5 or 2.
myDay.app.full: Pill on a group class row that has no places left.
myDay.app.openRoute: Accessibility label of the arrow that opens the maps app for a session's location.
myDay.app.removed: Notice, shown once, after the person lost access to a workspace.
myDay.app.scopeLabel: Accessibility label of the segmented control Mijn dag | Hele studio on Vandaag (the Owner of a workspace with a team).
myDay.app.scopeMine: Segment of the control on Vandaag: the Owner’s own day across workspaces.
myDay.app.scopeStudio: Segment of the control on Vandaag: the whole workspace’s day, one lane per trainer.
myDay.app.studioBlock: Accessible name of a session block in a trainer’s lane: {trainer}: {title} {start}.
myDay.app.studioBusiest: Head of the team card: the busiest moment of the day, {count} sessions at once.
myDay.app.studioLine: Line under the control on Hele studio; {words} is the workspace’s word for the people who teach.
myDay.app.studioNoOverlap: Head of the team card when no two sessions overlap.
myDay.app.studioNoTrainer: Label of the lane (and the row) of sessions that have no trainer yet.
myDay.app.studioTrainer: Line on the next card of Hele studio: {Word}: {name}; the name is Jij’s lowercase form for the Owner’s own session.
myDay.app.studioTrainersMany: Head of the team card with two or more people teaching today: {count} {words}, with the workspace’s word.
myDay.app.studioTrainersOne: Head of the team card with one person teaching today: {count} {word}, with the workspace’s word.
myDay.app.studioYou: Label of the signed-in Owner’s own lane on Hele studio.
myDay.app.studioYouLower: The Owner’s own session on the next card of Hele studio: Trainer: jij.
myDay.app.tab: Label of the first tab of Fivvi Pro: the trainer's day across workspaces.
myProfile.bookingEmailsLabel: Label of the checkbox on My profile (TW-09) that switches the emails for a client booking or cancelling in the person's own classes on or off (F050). On by default; the setting belongs to the account.
myProfile.editName: Title of the native dialog (iOS sheet, Android full-screen dialog) in which the person changes their name on Profile (TM-04), and the action of the name row that opens it.
myProfile.emailsTitle: Heading of the section of My profile (TW-09) with the switches for emails the person gets.
myProfile.title: Title of the page My profile (TW-09).
myProfile.workspacesTitle: Heading of the section listing the workspaces the person is on the team of, each with their role.
noAccess.body: Text of the no-access page (information-architecture §9.5, No permission). Native apps show it too, under the same conditions. The Dutch uses 'werkruimte' as the spec words it.
noAccess.title: Heading of the no-access page: a signed-in person who is not in a workspace and may not create one (a client, or someone who was removed). The page has the sign-out button.
noPermission.body: Text of the no-permission page. {workspace} is the name of the workspace, a name as typed by its owner and not translated.
noPermission.title: Heading of the no-permission page (information-architecture §9.5): a team member opens a page their role may not use, such as a Trainer opening Settings.
noWorkspace.haveLink: Second line of the no-workspace state in the client app: the join link opens in the app when it is tapped on this phone.
noWorkspace.teamHint: Third line of the no-workspace state, only for an account that is Owner or Trainer of a workspace: points to the trainer app (Fivvi Pro).
noWorkspace.title: Client app, Home and Boeken while the client belongs to no workspace: tells them to ask their studio for the join link. The wording is marked in GLOSSARY.md until the pilot gym owner confirms.
offers.cancellation.untilStart: The cancellation rule as clients read it, for a cutoff of 0 hours.
offers.cancellation.upTo: The cancellation rule as clients read it, for a cutoff of one hour or more. # is the number of hours.
offers.summary.classesPerWeek: Part of the one-line summary of a membership: the classes a week. # is the number.
offers.summary.creditsEveryFourWeeks: Part of the summary of a credit plan billed every 4 weeks. {credits} is the number of credits.
offers.summary.creditsEveryMonth: Part of the summary of a credit plan billed every month. {credits} is the number of credits, e.g. "4 privécredits".
offers.summary.days: Part of the summary of a credit pack: a validity in days.
offers.summary.deletedClass: A class an offer is limited to that was deleted later, still named on the offer's version. {name} is the class's name.
offers.summary.deletedClassUnnamed: A class an offer is limited to that was deleted with its name; the class is listed without a name.
offers.summary.groupCredits: Part of an offer summary: a number of group credits.
offers.summary.minimumTerm: Part of the summary of a credit plan. {duration} is a length in months, e.g. "3 maanden".
offers.summary.months: Part of an offer summary: a length in months (the term of a membership, the validity of a credit pack, the minimum term of a credit plan).
offers.summary.pricePerFourWeeks: Price of an offer billed every 4 weeks. {amount} is the amount including VAT.
offers.summary.pricePerMonth: Price of an offer billed every month. {amount} is the amount including VAT, e.g. "€ 79,00".
offers.summary.privateCredits: Part of an offer summary: a number of private credits.
offers.summary.singleClass: Part of the summary of a single class pass: what it is good for.
offers.summary.validFor: Part of the summary of a credit pack. {duration} is a length, e.g. "3 maanden".
offers.summary.weeks: Part of the summary of a credit pack: a validity in weeks.
personal.timeZoneHint: Shown on the personal pages when the browser is not in Dutch time: the times on the page are Dutch time.
profile.privacy: Row on the native Profile (iOS and Android, F064 AC17) that opens the privacy policy of the public website fivvi.app in the browser. Same wording as the website footer (site.footer.privacy).
profile.support: Row on the native Profile (iOS and Android, F064 AC17) that opens the Help and contact page of the public website fivvi.app in the browser. Same wording as the website footer (site.footer.support).
profile.trainsHere.errors.generic: Shown next to the switch when saving failed for another reason. The switch is back as it was.
profile.trainsHere.errors.noConnection: Shown next to the switch when saving failed because there is no connection. The switch is back as it was.
profile.trainsHere.label: Label of the switch on the profile (web My profile TW-09, iOS and Android Profile TM-04), one per workspace where the person is Owner. On means they also train there and show as a trainer (F005). {workspace} is the workspace name, e.g. John's Gym. It talks about training, never about profiles.
profile.trainsHere.saved: Confirmation shown after the switch was saved.
profile.version: Line at the end of the client app's Profiel with the app's version. {version} is the version number, e.g. '0.1.0'.
roles.owner: Role label of an Owner (Eigenaar) of a workspace, shown as a plain label.
roles.trainer: OLD role label of a Trainer, shown as a plain label with the literal word trainer. Kept until the web, iOS and Android use roles.trainerLabel (F068, ticket #751 removes it).
roles.trainerLabel: Role label of a Trainer of a workspace, shown as a plain label, in the workspace's word (F068): {Word} is the word with a capital start, e.g. Instructeur / Instructor. The role itself stays Trainer.
sessions.cancel.action: PS-06: the button on the session page (and the quick view) that opens the cancel dialog; it cancels the session, it does not dismiss anything. "Annuleren" / "Cancel" here is the cancel-the-session verb (GLOSSARY: Cancel / Annuleren), not the Cancel button of a dialog that closes it (common.cancel).
sessions.cancel.notifyNote: PS-06: under the notify box; {email} is the client's address, {language} the language of the email ("in het Nederlands" / "in het Engels", sessions.form.languageNl/languageEn).
sessions.cancel.offline: PS-06 in the apps: shown on the session page while the phone is offline, where the cancel action is disabled; nothing is queued. Les annuleren has its own text (classes.app.cancelOffline).
sessions.cancel.whoUs: PS-06: the workspace is cancelling (the initiator "workspace"); "Wij" in Dutch.
sessions.form.clientPlaceholder: The client row of the new private session form of the native apps, before a client is chosen. Tapping it opens the client list.
sessions.form.endsAt: Under the start time of the new private session form (PS-01): when the session ends, from the start and the duration. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. 10:00.
sessions.form.endsAtNextDay: Same as sessions.form.endsAt, when the session ends after midnight, on the next day.
sessions.form.errors.timeDoesNotExist: Shown under the start time when the clocks skip it because summer time starts (e.g. 02:30 on 28 March 2027). {date} is a full date.
sessions.form.languageEn: The language an email goes out in, after the client's address (sessions.form.notifyNote) and in a sentence (sessions.reschedule.notifyNote): "in English".
sessions.form.languageNl: The language an email goes out in, after the client's address (sessions.form.notifyNote) and in a sentence (sessions.reschedule.notifyNote): "in Dutch".
sessions.form.notes.past: Shown when the chosen start is before now. The session is saved afterwards, and the client gets no email.
sessions.form.notes.repeatedTime: Shown when the chosen time happens twice because the clocks go back at the end of summer time (e.g. 02:30 on 25 October 2026). The first one, in summer time, is used. {date} is a full date, {time} a 24-hour time.
sessions.form.notifyNote: Under the checkbox that sends the client a confirmation: the client's email address, then the language of the email, e.g. "anna@example.com · in het Nederlands".
sessions.form.offline: Shown on the new private session form of the native apps when the app can't reach the server; Save is off. Nothing is saved until the connection is back.
sessions.form.pickerDone: Confirm button of the date and the time picker of the session forms in the Android app.
sessions.form.saved: Message after a private session was saved. {client} is the client's name, {date} a short date such as "do 24 sep", {time} a 24-hour time.
sessions.form.workspaceLabel: Label of the first field of the private session form when it is opened from the personal calendar: the workspace the session is planned in. A plain line with one workspace.
sessions.page.more: Accessibility name of the ⋯ menu on the session screen of the native apps (Reschedule, Client profile).
sessions.page.moved: Message after a session was moved. {date} is a short date, {time} a 24-hour time.
sessions.page.route: Button on the session screen of the native apps, next to the location: opens the route to the location's address in the maps app.
sessions.page.you: On the session screen, the trainer row when the person looking is the trainer: "You" (Dutch "Jij"), instead of their name.
sessions.reschedule.changedBy: Shown when someone else changed or moved the session while this form was open. {name} is that person. The form then shows the session as it is now.
sessions.reschedule.current: Top of the reschedule dialog: where the session is now. {date} is a short date with the year, {start} and {end} are 24-hour times.
settingsGeneral.errors.generic: Shown on TW-08 when saving failed for any other reason. Nothing was changed.
settingsGeneral.errors.nameRequired: Under the name field on TW-08 when it is empty or only spaces.
settingsGeneral.errors.nameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-08 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
settingsGeneral.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-08 when the request to save could not reach the server. Nothing was changed.
settingsGeneral.nameLabel: Label of the workspace name field on TW-08. Same wording as the name field on the first-run screen.
settingsGeneral.save: Button of TW-08 that saves the new workspace name.
settingsGeneral.saved: Confirmation shown next to the save button on TW-08 after the name was saved.
settingsGeneral.timeZoneLabel: Label of the read-only time zone of the workspace on TW-08, shown with its IANA name, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam.
settingsGeneral.title: Heading and browser tab title of TW-08, Settings → General (`/w/{slug}/settings/general`, Owner only). Dutch: Algemeen.
settingsGeneral.urlNameLabel: Label of the read-only URL name of the workspace on TW-08 (the part of the web address and booking link made from the name at creation, which a rename never changes).
settingsLocation.additionLabel: Label of the optional house number addition field on TW-08, e.g. "A" or "2 hoog".
settingsLocation.addressLegend: Legend of the group of address fields on TW-08 (postcode, house number, addition, street, city). Optional: an address is all or nothing.
settingsLocation.cityLabel: Label of the city field on TW-08. The address lookup fills it in; the person can still type it.
settingsLocation.errors.addressIncomplet: Under the address fields on TW-08 when some but not all of postcode, house number, street and city are filled in.
settingsLocation.errors.generic: Shown on TW-08 when saving failed for any other reason. Nothing was changed.
settingsLocation.errors.houseNumberInval: Under the house number field on TW-08 when it is not one to five digits.
settingsLocation.errors.nameRequired: Under the name field on TW-08 when it is empty or only spaces.
settingsLocation.errors.nameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-08 when the name is over 120 characters. Same wording as the too-long workspace name.
settingsLocation.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-08 when the request to save could not reach the server. Nothing was changed.
settingsLocation.errors.postcodeInvalid: Under the postcode field on TW-08 when it is not a Dutch postcode (four digits, an optional space, two letters).
settingsLocation.errors.tooLong: Under the addition, street or city field on TW-08 when the text is over its limit.
settingsLocation.help: Help text under the heading of the location card on TW-08: every session and class takes the workspace's one location.
settingsLocation.houseNumberLabel: Label of the house number field on TW-08: one to five digits, no addition.
settingsLocation.lookup.busy: Shown on TW-08 while the street and city are looked up from the postcode and house number. The form stays usable.
settingsLocation.lookup.filled: Note on TW-08 under the address fields when the street and/or city were filled in by the address lookup.
settingsLocation.lookup.notFound: Shown on TW-08 when the lookup knows no address for the postcode and house number. Street and city stay empty for typing.
settingsLocation.lookup.unavailable: Shown on TW-08 when the address lookup timed out, failed or is used up for the hour. Saving a hand-typed address still works.
settingsLocation.nameLabel: Label of the location name field on TW-08. It is prefilled with the workspace name when the workspace is created.
settingsLocation.postcodeLabel: Label of the Dutch postcode field on TW-08, written like 1234 AB.
settingsLocation.save: Button of TW-08 that saves the location.
settingsLocation.saved: Confirmation shown next to the save button on TW-08 after the location was saved.
settingsLocation.streetLabel: Label of the street field on TW-08. The address lookup fills it in; the person can still type it.
settingsLocation.title: Heading and browser tab title of TW-08, Settings → Location (`/w/{slug}/settings/locations`, Owner only). Dutch: Locatie (GLOSSARY §4.3).
settingsLocation.typeLabel: Label of the read-only location type on TW-08 (Eigen locatie / Own location).
settingsLocation.types.organizationLocat: The type of the workspace's own location, shown read-only on TW-08 (GLOSSARY §4.3). The other types exist in the data model; they are not shown at go-live.
signIn.changeEmail: Button on the second step that goes back to the email field.
signIn.checkEmailBody: Under the heading of the second step. {email} is the address that was entered. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.checkEmailBodyApp: Native apps only (TM-01): under the heading of the code step, instead of signIn.checkEmailBody. {email} is the address entered. Says the email has a code, without the sign-in link: a link tapped on the phone signs in the phone's browser, not the app. The instruction to enter the code comes from signIn.codeHelp. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.checkEmailTitle: Heading of the second step of the sign-in page, shown after the email address was sent. Same wording whether or not the address has an account.
signIn.codeHelp: Helper text under the code field on the second step of the sign-in page. The field is described by it.
signIn.codeLabel: Label of the field for the 6-digit code from the email (one-time-code autofill on phones). The word alone; the sentence is signIn.codeHelp.
signIn.confirmChecking: Shown for a moment on the confirm step (TW-10) while the page checks the sign-in link from the email. Checking uses nothing up.
signIn.confirmSubmit: The one button of the confirm step. Pressing it uses up the link and signs this browser in.
signIn.confirmTitle: Heading of the confirm step, where the sign-in link from the email lands. {email} is the masked address the link signs in, e.g. j***@example.com.
signIn.emailLabel: Label of the email field on the sign-in page.
signIn.errors.generic: Shown when sign-in failed for any other reason.
signIn.errors.invalidEmail: Under the email field when the address is empty or not an email address.
signIn.errors.invalidOrExpiredCode: Shown when the code was refused. One message for a wrong, expired, used or replaced code: it never says which.
signIn.errors.noConnection: Shown when the sign-in request could not reach the server.
signIn.linkInvalidBack: Button on the confirm step for a link that no longer works. Goes back to the sign-in page, where a new email is requested.
signIn.linkInvalidBody: Line under signIn.linkInvalidTitle, pointing to the button that goes back to the sign-in page.
signIn.linkInvalidTitle: Heading of the confirm step when the link no longer works. One message for an expired, used or replaced link: it never says which.
signIn.resend: Button on the second step that sends a new email. The new code replaces the old one.
signIn.resent: Confirmation after a new email was requested. {email} is the address entered. Does not say whether an account exists.
signIn.sendCode: Button under the email field of the sign-in page. Sends one email with a 6-digit code and a sign-in link.
signIn.signedOutNotice: Native apps only: notice at the top of the sign-in screen (TM-01) when the app was signed out without the person asking: the server no longer accepts the stored sign-in, or the person signed out elsewhere. Not shown after the person signs out in the app.
signIn.submitCode: Button that signs in with the code that was entered.
signIn.title: Heading of the first step of the sign-in page (TW-10), where the email address is entered, and the browser tab title of the page.
signOut.error: Shown next to the sign-out button when signing out failed (no connection or a server error). The person is still signed in and can try again.
signOut.label: Button that signs out only the browser (or device) it is pressed on; other browsers stay signed in. On every signed-in page of the web app.
team.actionsColumn: Header of the last column of the team list, which holds the row action. Only read aloud by screen readers.
team.badge.trainer: Badge on a team member of the Trainers page (TW-06) who trains in the workspace, next to their role label. The word for the role Trainer.
team.emailColumn: Column header of the email address in the team list.
team.errors.generic: Shown on the Trainers page when removing a person failed for another reason. Nothing changed.
team.errors.noConnection: Shown on the Trainers page when removing a person failed because there is no connection. Nothing changed.
team.nameColumn: Column header of the person's name in the team list.
team.remove: Row action of a Trainer in the team list. Opens the remove dialog; the team access ends only after the Owner confirms there.
team.removeDialog.body: Body of the remove dialog. {name} is the person's name, repeated instead of a pronoun; {workspace} the workspace name. Says that only the team access goes and what they have as a client stays.
team.removeDialog.cancel: Dismiss button of the remove dialog. Closes it without removing anyone.
team.removeDialog.confirm: Destructive button of the remove dialog. Removes the person from the team.
team.removeDialog.title: Title of the remove dialog, a question. {name} is the person's name (or email address when they have no name). No pronoun: the product does not know anyone's pronouns.
team.removed: Confirmation shown after a person was removed from the team. {name} is the person's name (or email address when they have no name).
team.roleColumn: Column header of the role label (Owner or Trainer) in the team list.
team.title: Title of the Trainers page (TW-06), which lists the team of the workspace, and its browser tab title.
trainerWord.coach.aWord: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the singular with its article, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {aWord}); English chooses a or an. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.coach.aWordCap: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the singular with its article and a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {AWord}); English chooses A or An. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.coach.word: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the singular, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.coach.wordCap: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the singular with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.coach.words: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the plural, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.coach.wordsCap: The workspace's word 'coach' (F068), the plural with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.aWord: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the singular with its article, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {aWord}); English chooses a or an. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.aWordCap: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the singular with its article and a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {AWord}); English chooses A or An. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.word: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the singular, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.wordCap: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the singular with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.words: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the plural, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.docent.wordsCap: The workspace's word 'docent / teacher' (F068), the plural with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.aWord: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the singular with its article, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {aWord}); English chooses a or an. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.aWordCap: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the singular with its article and a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {AWord}); English chooses A or An. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.word: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the singular, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.wordCap: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the singular with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.words: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the plural, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.instructeur.wordsCap: The workspace's word 'instructeur / instructor' (F068), the plural with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.aWord: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the singular with its article, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {aWord}); English chooses a or an. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.aWordCap: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the singular with its article and a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {AWord}); English chooses A or An. One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.word: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the singular, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.wordCap: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the singular with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Word}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.words: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the plural, lowercase, for use inside a sentence (placeholder {words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
trainerWord.trainer.wordsCap: The workspace's word 'trainer' (F068), the plural with a capital start, for the start of a message (placeholder {Words}). One of six forms of the word; the apps pass them as placeholders (trainerWordForms).
userMenu.error: Shown in the user menu when the chosen language could not be saved on the account (no connection or a server error). The page keeps its language and the person can try again.
userMenu.label: Accessible name of the button that opens the user menu (the ⋯ button) in the frame of a workspace's pages.
userMenu.language: Menu row that opens the two language options; {language} is the current language written in its own language (Nederlands or English).
userMenu.languageEn: Language option, always written in English whatever the interface language (GLOSSARY §4.8).
userMenu.languageNl: Language option, always written in Dutch whatever the interface language (GLOSSARY §4.8).
userMenu.profile: Menu link to the page My profile (TW-09), where the person sees the workspaces they are on the team of.
welcome.description: Line under the heading of TW-11.
welcome.errors.generic: Shown on TW-11 when creating the workspace failed for any other reason. Nothing was created.
welcome.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-11 when the request to create the workspace could not reach the server. Nothing was created.
welcome.errors.personNameRequired: Under the name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.personNameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.errors.workspaceNameRequired: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.workspaceNameTooLong: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.personNameLabel: Label of the field for the person's own name on TW-11. Shown only when the account has no name yet.
welcome.submit: Submit button of TW-11. It creates the workspace and opens it.
welcome.title: Heading of TW-11, the first-run screen (`/welcome`) shown once to an operator-approved person who has no workspace yet. Fivvi is the product name.
welcome.workspaceNameHint: Hint under the workspace name field on TW-11: an example of a name. "John's Gym" is a name, the same in both languages.
welcome.workspaceNameLabel: Label of the field for the name of the gym or business on TW-11. The workspace itself, worded as the person's own business (GLOSSARY §4.1: prefer this over the word werkruimte).
workspaceDashboard.addGroup: Button of the new-workspace welcome on the Dashboard (WC-01) that opens the dialog to plan a class date (F021). Group class: the glossary word for a class (groepsles).
workspaceDashboard.addPrivate: Button of the new-workspace welcome on the Dashboard (WC-01) that opens the dialog to plan a private session (PS-01).
workspaceDashboard.assign: Button of an Aandacht nodig row that opens the session to give it a trainer (GLOSSARY §4.1: toewijzen, never koppelen).
workspaceDashboard.assignLabel: Accessible name of the Toewijzen button: the word first, then the row it belongs to.
workspaceDashboard.attentionNoTrainer: A row of Aandacht nodig: a class date or private session in the next 14 days without a trainer. {name} is "Boxing" or "Privé · Mark Jansen", {date} and {time} the day and start time. {word} is the workspace's word for the people who teach (F068).
workspaceDashboard.blockDetail: Second line of a class block in the lanes: the start time and the places taken, e.g. "10:00 · 3/8". Keep the separator.
workspaceDashboard.columnOccupancy: Column of Nog vandaag: places taken of a class, or the location of a private session.
workspaceDashboard.emptyDay: Shown on the Dashboard when nothing is scheduled today. {workspace} is the workspace name.
workspaceDashboard.fraction: A count out of a total on a tile, e.g. 3/5. Keep the slash.
workspaceDashboard.groupBooked: Small text under the places count on the Groepsplekken tile: "7/8 geboekt".
workspaceDashboard.lanesNote: Under the title of the lanes card. {word} is the workspace's word for the people who teach (F068).
workspaceDashboard.scopeLabel: Accessible name of the switch between the Owner's own day (Mijn dag) and the workspace's day.
workspaceDashboard.sessionsDone: Small text under the done count on the Sessies vandaag tile: "3/5 klaar".
workspaceDashboard.title: Page title of the Owner's home of a workspace (WC-01), the Dashboard. A loanword both languages use.
workspaceDashboard.today: Line above the Dashboard: "VANDAAG · DINSDAG 22 SEPTEMBER" (the screen sets it in capitals). {date} is the weekday and date in the reader's language.
workspaceDashboard.welcome: Shown on the Dashboard of a new workspace, where nothing has ever been planned, instead of the empty-day text (WC-01). Two sentences; the second points at the two buttons that follow (class timetable, private session).
workspaceNav.label: Accessible name of the navigation of a workspace's pages, read by screen readers.
workspaceNav.settings: Navigation link to Settings (Instellingen). Shown to the Owner only (GLOSSARY §4.8).
workspaceNav.settingsLocation: Navigation link to Settings → Location (TW-08). Shown to the Owner only.
workspaceNav.trainers: Navigation link to the Trainers page (TW-06), the team list. Shown to the Owner only.
workspaceNav.workspaceWithRole: Header of the sidebar: the workspace name, then the role of the signed-in person in it, e.g. "John's Gym · Owner". {name} is the workspace name, {role} the role label.
workspaceSwitcher.newWorkspace: Last row of the scope switcher, only for accounts that may set up a workspace (the sign-up allowlist): opens the form to create another workspace. The + belongs to the label.
